tooltip.title: Dermatitis Herpetiformis (DH)
tooltip.markdown: The cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease (gluten sensitivity). Characterized by intensely pruritic vesicles and papules.

tooltip.title: Pathophysiology of DH
tooltip.markdown: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of dermatitis herpetiformis

tooltip.title: Mechanism
tooltip.markdown: Ingestion of gluten leads to production of IgA autoantibodies against tissue transglutaminase (tTG) and epidermal transglutaminase (eTG)

tooltip.title: Deposition
tooltip.markdown: IgA-eTG immune complexes deposit in the dermal papillae, recruiting neutrophils and causing blistering

tooltip.title: Clinical Features of DH
tooltip.markdown: Key clinical manifestations and physical findings

tooltip.title: Symptoms
tooltip.markdown: Intense, burning pruritus is the hallmark symptom

tooltip.title: Lesions
tooltip.markdown: Grouped ("herpetiform") vesicles, papules, and urticarial plaques. Often excoriated and difficult to see intact blisters

tooltip.title: Distribution
tooltip.markdown: Symmetrical involvement of extensor surfaces (elbows, knees), buttocks, and posterior scalp

tooltip.title: Histology
tooltip.markdown: Neutrophilic microabscesses in the dermal papillae

tooltip.title: Direct Immunofluorescence
tooltip.markdown: The gold standard. Shows granular IgA deposition in the dermal papillae

tooltip.title: Serology
tooltip.markdown: Positive serology for anti-tTG and anti-endomysial IgA antibodies confirms underlying celiac disease

tooltip.title: Dietary Treatment
tooltip.markdown: A strict, lifelong gluten-free diet is the primary treatment and manages both skin and gut disease

tooltip.title: Pharmacologic Treatment
tooltip.markdown: Dapsone provides rapid relief of pruritus and skin lesions but does not treat the underlying intestinal disease
